extracted.intended_audience: antibiotic drug developers, preclinical researchers, and grant reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating ADEP4/antibiotic combination therapies in vitro and in vivo, including PK/PD characterization, resistance-frequency testing, toxicity screening, and criteria for advancement toward pre-IND development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterilization / eradication endpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete sterilization is defined as no colonies detected after treatment, i.e., eradication of cells in the biofilm or infected tissue to the limit of detection (including plating the entire thigh homogenate when applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ‘No colonies were detected ... after 72 h of incubating stationary cultures with the combination of ADEP4 and rifampicin.’ ‘*No cell counts were present in the ADEP + rifampicin group, even when the entire thigh homogenate from each animal was plated.’ Use plating of entire homogenate and report limit of detection. Re-growth testing (replace antibiotics with fresh medium) can confirm complete eradication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance-frequency threshold for advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Combinations advancing beyond Phase I should demonstrate a frequency of resistance development below 10^-9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milestone: ‘Identify ADEP4/antibiotic combinations which sterilize MRSA in stationary, biofilm and hollow fiber models, and have a frequency of resistance development <10^-9.’ Combinations with resistance rate <10^-9 are considered acceptable for further advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of combinations to minimize resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale and expected reduction in probability of resistance when pairing ADEP4 with partner antibiotics based on individual resistance frequencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example calculation: clpP null mutants arise ~10^-6; rifampicin resistance ~10^-8; combination resistance estimated ~10^-14. Nevertheless, measure resistance under varied drug exposures because changing concentrations can promote resistance (inverted-U relationship).

rubrics_metrics.name: PKPD driver candidates and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: For antiinfectives, the PKPD driver is generally one of: fAUC/MIC, fT>MIC, or fCMax/MIC. The PKPD driver for ADEP4 in combination with an antibiotic must be experimentally determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: determine PK of agents, dose-fractionate to create a range of AUC/T>MIC/CMax values, treat groups, then plot pathogen counts against AUC, T>MIC and CMax to identify which parameter correlates most closely with efficacy. Example: ‘if PKPD driver is fAUC/MIC of 100… deliver total 24h fAUC of 400 µg.h/mL.’

rubrics_metrics.name: Hollow-fiber infection model as resistance/sterilization assay
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the hollow-fiber pharmacodynamic system to simulate human-relevant drug exposures, half-lives, and to monitor sterilization and resistance emergence over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model specifics: pathogen grows in a chamber separated by semi-permeable membrane; nutrients and drugs pass but not cells; pump fresh media/drugs into central compartment; sample ports allow monitoring drug concentrations and culture densities. Deliver antibiotic concentrations based on physiologically relevant human concentrations adjusted for protein binding. Example result: ‘No cell counts were present after 24 hours’ and no resistance over 4 days for ADEP+rifampicin in preliminary experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro exposure parameters for bactericidal testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clinically achievable concentrations and multiples of MIC for in vitro stationary-phase and biofilm killing assays (e.g., 10× MIC), with specified incubation times and endpoint plating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example assays: stationary cultures exposed to 10× MIC for 2 days; biofilms exposed to antibiotics at 10× MIC for 24 and 72 hours, then washed, sonicated and plated for colony counts. Report error bars, independent experiment replicates, and detection limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biofilm testing models and their use
rubrics_metrics.description: Test combinations against biofilms using multiple complementary in vitro and in vivo biofilm models: Calgary™ device, flow cell biofilm model, and implanted tissue-cage (TC) mouse biofilm model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calgary device: peg-based biofilms in suspension. Flow cell: better resembles in vivo shear flow. In vivo TC model: sintered glass bead cage implanted subcutaneously, infection allowed to stabilize for 14 days, dose for 7 days, then quantify TC fluid and beads (wash + sonication). Use 10 mice/group and include 20% excess due to variability and sterility failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety/ADME/DMPK screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Screen ADEP4/antibiotic combinations against a safety panel of human enzymes, receptors, and major CYP450s to detect adverse secondary drug interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Eurofins lead profiling + CYP screening (68 targets + 5 CYPs). Test combinations in duplicate at 10 µM and flag any inhibition >50% vs negative controls. Confirm hits in dose-response follow-ups comparing each component vs combination. Deprioritize combinations showing significantly higher adverse activity than either agent alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxicity and MTD constraints in dosing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not test ADEP4 doses above the published maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Use MTD-informed dose ranges and avoid exceeding established safety limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published MTD for ADEP4 = 100 mg/kg; 50 mg/kg sterilized in mouse model and was used as an efficacious starting dose. Dose ratios planned include 1:1, 2:1 and 3:1 (ADEP:rifampicin) corresponding to 30, 60 and 90 mg/kg. ‘ADEP4 doses above the MTD will not be tested.’

rubrics_metrics.name: Dose-fractionation / regimen optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate multiple dosing schedules (q24h, q12h, q8h, q6h) across different mg/kg levels to generate a broad range of AUC, T>MIC and CMax for PKPD analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design: groups of 5 mice per regimen; include fractions such as 0.5x, 1x, 2x and 4x around an efficacious dose; total mice for dose fractionation example = 105. Use results to determine PKPD driver and optimize dosing frequency vs dose.

rubrics_metrics.name: PK study design and PK parameters to measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine pharmacokinetics of ADEP4 (and combinations) via IV and IP routes at multiple dose levels with serial micro-sampling and LC-MS/MS quantification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: IV/IP dosing at 25, 50 and 100 mg/kg; serial blood sampling at 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 270, 480 and 1440 minutes (microsampling from submandibular bleeds); measure oral bioavailability, elimination half-life, CMax, AUC, and T>MIC. Use PK data to adjust dosing strategy for efficacy experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial efficacy study design and control groups
rubrics_metrics.description: For murine thigh infection efficacy studies include vehicle control, antibiotic alone, ADEP4 alone, antibiotic + ADEP4, and positive control (ADEP4 + rifampicin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example group sizes: 5 mice per group with ~10% excess; dosing: initial ADEP4 50 mg/kg (½ MTD) with standard partner antibiotic dose adjusted based on combined PK. Report sample numbers, routes, and endpoints (thigh burden plated after euthanasia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance testing protocol in hollow-fiber and plate-based assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure frequency and dynamics of resistance emergence under prolonged exposure, multiple drug ratios, and plate on selective agar to identify resistant subpopulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand experiments to 10 days and test 3 different ADEP4/partner antibiotic ratios. Collect samples from hollow-fiber chamber over time, wash/dilute/plate for total live counts, and plate aliquots on agar containing 3× MIC of each drug to detect resistant subpopulations and determine frequency. Consider inverted-U relationship between exposure and resistance when designing concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for deprioritizing combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprioritize any ADEP4/antibiotic combinations that show unacceptable toxicity, significant adverse activity in safety profiling, or high rates of resistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: combinations showing >50% inhibition on safety panel without acceptable confirmatory profiles, combinations showing higher adverse activity than single agents, or combinations with resistance frequencies >10^-9 will be deprioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclinical development package required for pre-IND
rubrics_metrics.description: Before pre-IND discussions, perform standard preclinical studies: acute and repeated dose toxicity in two species, single dose PK in two species, genotoxicity (Ames and chromosomal aberration), and local irritation assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outsource GLP studies to CRO. Example plans: single dose MTD in rats (24 rats, 3/sex/group), 7-day repeat dose range-finding, and 14-day GLP repeat dose toxicity in Sprague Dawley rats (10 males + 10 females per group, vehicle controls included). Collect clinical pathology, necropsy, organ weights, and histopathology per ICH/OECD guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genotoxicity testing specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess genotoxic potential using the Ames reverse mutation assay and chromosomal aberration assays in mammalian cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ames: use strains of Salmonella (His-) and E. coli (Trp-), test 6 concentrations of ADEP4/partner combination and count revertants vs controls. Chromosomal aberration: test CHO cell line at three concentrations and human lymphocytes; examine metaphase cells for structural aberrations and perform confirmatory assays with extended exposure if initial results are negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal model parameters and welfare constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Define species/strain/sex/ages/numbers, immunosuppression regimen, infection inocula, timing of therapy, blood draw limits, and IACUC approvals for animal studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: neutropenic murine thigh model uses cyclophosphamide to induce neutropenia, infect with 1x10^6 cells and allow 24h before treatment to model recalcitrant infection. PK mice: 6-8 week old female C57BL/6 for PK. Blood draws via submandibular bleed not to exceed IACUC volume guidelines; euthanize at 1440 min for terminal bleed. Include institutional IACUC approval dates and assurance numbers in documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of human-equivalent exposure calculations for in vitro/in silico modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate human dosing regimens into experimental concentrations (e.g., hollow-fiber) by adjusting for protein binding and using human standard dose regimens to set concentration-time profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: antibiotic concentrations in hollow-fiber were based on physiologically relevant concentrations achieved in humans and adjusted for protein binding; ADEP concentrations used mouse PK AUC scaled to effective dose (AUC multiplied by 10 to estimate 50 mg/kg from 5 mg/kg mouse IV), assuming linearity and then adjusted for protein binding.
